commentaries.whitney: Stand, a man ( púmāṅs ), upon men; go to the hide; call thither her who is dear to thee; of what age (? yā́vant ) ye two first came together in the beginning, let that be your same age in Yama's realm.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines puṅso adhi and omits ihi in a . Kāuç. 60. 31 has the verse used when the sacrificer is made to stand upon the ox-hide which is to be his station during the ceremony. The various antecedents have been prepared to the accompaniment of the first verses of xi. 1.

commentaries.whitney: So much [be] your sight, so many your powers ( vīryà ), so great your brilliancy ( téjas ), so many-fold your energies ( vā́jina ); Agni fastens on ( sac ) the body when [it is his] fuel (?); then, O paired ones ( mithuná ), shall ye come into being from what is cooked ( pakvá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text has yadā́: édhaḥ in c , as translated. Ppp. reads before it agniṁ çarīraṁ sajate , and after it atha; and in a, b it makes cakṣus and tejas change places. ⌊In OB. V. 258, pakvá is defined as 'the charred remains and ashes of a corpse.' Pāda d recurs in vs. 9.⌋ ⌊W. makes a query on the margin: "the husband and wife burnt together?? and born anew and alike out of the cremation?"⌋

commentaries.whitney: Together in this world, together on the [road] the gods travel, together also unite ye (du.) in the realms of Yama; purified by purifiers, call ye to yourselves whatever seed ( rétas ) came into being from you.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Partly prose—namely parts of vss. 55-60.⌋ Found also ⌊except vs. 28⌋ in Pāipp. xvii. (with slight differences of verse-order, noted under the verses). Nearly all the verses of the hymn are used, according to Kāuç. 60-63, and on the whole in their natural order, and combined especially with xi. 1 (often a verse from each hymn being quoted in the same rule), in the sava ceremony; very few verses anywhere else. Vāit. quotes only 4 verses. All the mss. agree in the unaccented asmin in a . The verse appears to be quoted (as 'third verse') in Kāuç. 60. 33, to accompany a calling upon their offspring ( apatya ).

commentaries.whitney: Enter together, ye sons, into the waters, coming together, ye rich in life, unto this living one (m.); of them (f.) share ye the one which (m.) they call immortal, the rice-dish which your (du.) generatrix cooks.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The meaning and connection are very obscure. 'Of them' seems to refer to the waters (f.). Ppp. removes one difficulty by reading vas instead of vām in d ; it has in b ⌊ -dhanyāt ⌋ sametā ⌊cf. vs. 25⌋. In Kāuç. 60. 35 the verse is used when the pair lie down together, accompanied by their offspring, after a vessel of water has been set on the hide.

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads at the beginning yaṁ vaṣ pitā .

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines in c yo ‘gre , and part of our mss. (P.M.W.T.) read the same.

commentaries.whitney: Take ye (du.) hold upon each forward direction; to this world they that have faith attach themselves ( sac ); what of you that is cooked is served up in the fire, combine ye, O husband-and-wife, in order to its guarding.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse is nearly accordant with vi. 122. 3. 'Forward' ( prañc ) is also 'eastern.' ⌊Note here again the sequence of the cardinal points ( pradakṣiṇa ), and cf. end of introd. to iii. 26.⌋ The Anukr. passes the irregularity of the second half-verse (11 + 11: 10 + 12 = 44) without notice. Kāuç. 61. 1 quotes this verse alone; and 61. 2 quotes 7-10 as used while they follow around the vessel of water. Ppp. reads, for c, d , as follows: mimāthāṁ pātṛ tad vāṁ pūrṇam astu çivāṁ pakvaṣ pitryāyaṇ ‘ty ( ‘bhy? ) āmayat .

commentaries.whitney: Attaining unto the southern quarter, turn ye (du.) about unto this vessel; in it shall Yama, in concord with the Fathers, assure abundant protection unto your cooked [offering].
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'In it': i.e., as the gender shows, in the vessel. Some of our mss. make very bad work with vām in c , reading vāyám (P.M.W.), vayám (Bs.s.m.), varā́m (R.), vāṁ yam (T.). It is absurd of the Anukr. to reckon the verse (11 + 11: 12 + 11 = 45) a jagatī .

commentaries.whitney: This western of the quarters verily is a thing to be preferred, in which Soma is over-ruler and favorer; to it resort ( çri ) ye (du.); attach yourselves to the well-doers; then, O paired ones, shall ye come into being from what is cooked.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last pāda is identical with 2 d above. But Ppp. reads instead adhā pakvena saha saṁ bhavema , which is nearly identical with vi. 119. 2 d and the concluding pāda of SS-60 below. The Anukr. takes no notice of the deficiency of the first pāda.

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads pan̄ktiç chandaṣ at the beginning of c . We have to resolve pa-ān- in order to make a full pāda.

commentaries.whitney: This fixed [quarter] is virā́j; homage be to it; let it be propitious to [my] sons and to me; do thou, O goddess Aditi, having all choice things, like an active herdsman defend our cooked [offering].
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse is quoted in Kāuç. 61. 3, next after the four preceding ones.

items.samhita_patha: पि॒तेव॑ पु॒त्रान॒भि सं स्व॑जस्व नः शि॒वा नो॒ वाता॑ इ॒ह वा॑न्तु॒ भूमौ॑। यमो॑द॒नं पच॑तो दे॒वते॑ इ॒ह तं न॒स्तप॑ उ॒त स॒त्यं च॑ वेत्तु ॥

commentaries.whitney: Do thou embrace us, as a father his sons; let propitious winds blow here for us on the earth; what rice-dish the two deities cook here, let that know our penance and also truth.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads çagdā for bhūmāu in b , and vittam for vettu at the end. 'That' ( tát ) in d is neuter, and so not correlative to 'what' ( yám m.) in c . P.M.W. read svaja naḥ at end of a . The verse lacks two syllables of being a good jagatī . ⌊The verse is quoted at Kāuç. 61. 4.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: पितेव पुत्रानभि सं स्वजस्व नः शिवा नो वाता इह वान्तु भूमौ। यमोदनं पचतो देवते इह तं नस्तप उत सत्यं च वेत्तु ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whenever the black bird, coming hither, hath sat upon the orifice, surprising ( tsar ) what is resolved ( vi-sañj ), or when the barbarian woman ( dāsī́ ) with wet hands smears over—cleanse, ye waters, the mortar [and] pestle.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines in a çakune ’ha , and reads in c dāsī vā yad , and in d ⌊cf. vss. 21 and 26 and note to vi. 115. 3⌋ çundhatā ”paḥ . Kāuç. quotes the verse in 8. 14, and the coram, also under 2. 6, but they cast no light on the obscure first half-verse. The verse is a good triṣṭubh , yet the Anukr. attempts to give it some special description, of which the text is corrupt and unintelligible ( yad-yat kṛṣṇa ity āthā ).

commentaries.whitney: Let this pressing-stone, broad-based, vigor-bestowing, purified by purifiers, smite away the demon; mount thou the hide; yield great protection; let not the husband-and-wife fall into evil proceeding from sons ( pāútra ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has at the end gāthām , with which, of course, dampatī would have to be understood as vocative, unaccented. Expressions like that in d are found in several of the Sūtras: in AGS. i. 13. 7, mā ’ham pāutram aghaṁ ni yām (should be gām, probably); in PGS. i. 5. 11, yathe ’yaṁ strī pāutram aghaṁ na rodāt; and the same in HGS. i. 19. 7, with pāutram ānandam as antithesis to it. The verse is quoted in Kāuç. 61. 18 (in connection with xi. 1. 9), to accompany the setting of mortar, pestle, and winnowing basket, after sprinkling, upon the hide.

items.samhita_patha: वन॒स्पतिः॑ स॒ह दे॒वैर्न॒ आग॒न्रक्षः॑ पिशा॒चाँ अ॑प॒बाध॑मानः। स उच्छ्र॑यातै॒ प्र व॑दाति॒ वाचं॒ तेन॑ लो॒काँ अ॒भि सर्वा॑ञ्जयेम ॥

commentaries.whitney: The forest tree hath come to us together with the gods, forcing off the demon, the piçācás; he shall rise up ( ut-çri ), shall speak forth his voice; with him may we conquer all worlds.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads and combines sāu ’cchrāyātāi in c , and reads api for abhi in d . According to Kāuç. 61. 21, one sets up the pestle with this verse; in 125. 3 the verse is used with reference to the sacrificial post ⌊in case it puts forth fresh shoots⌋; and similarly in Vāit. 10. 8 ⌊in the paçubandha ⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: वनस्पतिः सह देवैर्न आगन्रक्षः पिशाचाँ अपबाधमानः। स उच्छ्रयातै प्र वदाति वाचं तेन लोकाँ अभि सर्वाञ्जयेम ॥

commentaries.whitney: Seven sacrifices ( médha ) the cattle enclosed—which ⌊ the relative pronoun ⌋ of them was full of light, and which was pining; to them thirty deities attach themselves; do thou (m.) conduct us (pl.) unto the heavenly ( svargá ) world.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Our Bp. reads tarn in c , and a few of the saṁhitā -mss. (P.M.W.E.) agree with it; tā́m is certainly wrong, but tám would be an acceptable improvement. Ppp. has medhasvān instead of jyotiṣmān (and the latter must be taken as having the sense of the former); also cakarṣa in b , and neṣi in d . ⌊For neṣa , see Gram. § 896.⌋ The verse is quoted in Kāuç. 61. 13, to accompany the handling or stroking of something by the two spouses ⌊with their offspring⌋. Pāda b has a redundant syllable, unnoticed by the Anukr., unless we contract to yāi ’ṣām .

items.samhita_patha: स्व॒र्गं लो॒कम॒भि नो॑ नयासि॒ सं जा॒यया॑ स॒ह पु॒त्रैः स्या॑म। गृ॒ह्णामि॒ हस्त॒मनु॒ मैत्वत्र॒ मा न॑स्तारी॒न्निरृ॑ति॒र्मो अरा॑तिः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Unto the heavenly world shalt thou conduct us (pl.); may we be united with wife, with sons; I grasp [her (?)] hand; let her (?) come here after me; let not destruction pass us, nor the niggard.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last pāda is nearly the same with vi. 124. 3 d ; cf. also ii. 7. 4 c, d . Ppp. ends d with no ‘rātiḥ . The verse is a good triṣṭubh , and its description by the Anukr. is absurd. Kāuç. 61. 14 uses the latter half-verse, not in a way to cast light on its meaning.

items.samhita_patha_plain: स्वर्गं लोकमभि नो नयासि सं जायया सह पुत्रैः स्याम। गृह्णामि हस्तमनु मैत्वत्र मा नस्तारीन्निरृतिर्मो अरातिः ॥

items.samhita_patha: ग्राहिं॑ पा॒प्मान॒मति॒ ताँ अ॑याम॒ तमो॒ व्य᳡स्य॒ प्र व॑दासि व॒ल्गु। वा॑नस्प॒त्य उद्य॑तो॒ मा जि॑हिंसी॒र्मा त॑ण्डु॒लं वि श॑रीर्देव॒यन्त॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: The seizure ( grā́hi ), evil ( pāpmán )—may we go beyond them (pl.); dissipate thou the darkness; mayest thou speak forth what is agreeable; made of forest tree, uplifted, do not injure; do not crush to pieces ⌊ vi-çṛ ⌋ the god-loving rice-grain.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Jihiṅsīr in c is a misprint fox jíhiṅsīr , which all the ⌊i.e. W's⌋ mss. read. ⌊So read 9 of SPP's authorities: and 4 have jáhiṅsīs; but SPP. prints jihiṅsīs , accentless, with 3 of his mss. Perhaps the accent is to be regarded as antithetical.⌋ A part of our mss. (O.T.K.D.R.p.m.) read çarīs in d ; Ppp. has çarāis ⌊see the references under vi. 32. 2⌋. The verse (with xi. 1. 9 b ) accompanies in Kāuç. 61. 22 the pounding with the pestle.

commentaries.whitney: About to become all-expanded, ghee-backed, go thou, of like origin ( sáyoni ), unto that world; hand thou ( upa-yam ) the rain-increased sieve; let that winnow away the husk, the chaff.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first half-verse is identical with 53 c, d below. Some mss. (I.O.D.K.: also half of the Kāuç. mss.) read palā́vām in d . Ppp. has vidvān instead of etam in b . With c , according to Kāuç. 61. 23, the çūrpa is grasped; with a (or the whole verse?), according to 24, it is raised; with d , according to 25, the sifting is done. The third pāda lacks a syllable, unless we may resolve çu-úrpam . ⌊For "sieve," here and in vs. 20, read rather "winnowing-basket"?⌋

commentaries.whitney: The three worlds are commensurate with the brā́hmaṇa: yon heaven, namely, earth, atmosphere; having seized the [soma-] stalks, take ye (du.) hold after; let them swell up ( ā-pyā ); let them come again to the sieve.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All our mss. (except D.) read asāu , unaccented, in b ; emendation to asāú was plainly necessary. All the saṁhitā -mss. (except E.) separate in c gṛbhītvā́ anv- , which, accordingly, might perhaps as well have been left, though the Prāt. does not recognize the case of irregular hiatus. Ppp. seems to combine the two words in the usual fashion; but it has -rabhetām; also, in b , pṛthivyām ant- . The verse is quoted in Kāuç. 61. 27 in connection with touching the winnowed grains (?); and, in 28, the last words of d ( punar etc.), with scattering them, apparently, again on the sieve.

items.samhita_patha_plain: त्रयो लोकाः संमिता ब्राह्मणेन द्यौरेवासौ पृथिव्य१न्तरिक्षम्। अंशून्गृभीत्वान्वारभेथामा प्यायन्तां पुनरा यन्तु शूर्पम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: पृथ॑ग्रू॒पाणि॑ बहु॒धा प॑शू॒नामेक॑रूपो भवसि॒ सं समृ॑द्ध्या। ए॒तां त्वचं॒ लोहि॑नीं॒ तां नु॑दस्व॒ ग्रावा॑ शुम्भाति मल॒ग इ॑व॒ वस्त्रा॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Manifoldly separate [are] the forms of cattle; thou becomest one-formed together with success; that red skin—that thrust thou [away]; the pressing-stone shall cleanse like a fuller (? malagá ) the garments.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Or b may be 'thou comest into being one-formed with success.' Malagá occurs nowhere else; its use with iva makes it impossible to tell whether the pada -text would divide mala॰gaḥ . Ppp. reads bhavati in b and malagāi ’va in d . ⌊Again, as in vss. 13 and 26, it reads çundhāti for çumbhāti : cf. note to vi. 115. 3.⌋ The quotation in Kāuç. 61. 26 casts no light on the meaning. Our text ought to read sámṛddhyā at end of b . The verse is very ill named jagatī by the Anukr.; the treatment of iva in d as only one syllable makes a regular triṣṭubh of it.

items.samhita_patha_plain: पृथग्रूपाणि बहुधा पशूनामेकरूपो भवसि सं समृद्ध्या। एतां त्वचं लोहिनीं तां नुदस्व ग्रावा शुम्भाति मलग इव वस्त्रा ॥

items.samhita_patha: पृ॑थि॒वीं त्वा॑ पृथि॒व्यामा वे॑शयामि त॒नूः स॑मा॒नी विकृ॑ता त ए॒षा। यद्य॑द्द्यु॒त्तं लि॑खि॒तमर्प॑णेन॒ तेन॒ मा सु॑स्रो॒र्ब्रह्म॒णापि॒ तद्व॑पामि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thee that art earth I make enter into earth; this like body of thee [is] separated; whatever of thee is burnt (? dyuttá ), [or] scratched by driving ( árpaṇa ); with that do not leak; I cover that over by a spell ( bráhman ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for a , bhūmyāṁ bhūmim adhi dhārayāmi; in c , arpaṇaṁ ca; in d , çuçror apa tad , thus restoring the meter. The verse (12 + 11: 11 + 13 = 47) is very ill defined simply as a jagatī . In Kāuç. 61. 30, the verse accompanies the smearing of a vessel ( kumbhī ); in Vāit. 28. 12, the fashioning of a kettle.

items.samhita_patha_plain: पृथिवीं त्वा पृथिव्यामा वेशयामि तनूः समानी विकृता त एषा। यद्यद्द्युत्तं लिखितमर्पणेन तेन मा सुस्रोर्ब्रह्मणापि तद्वपामि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Mayest thou welcome as a mother a son; I unite ( sam-dhā ) thee that art earth with the earth; a kettle, a vessel, do not stagger upon the sacrificial hearth, overhung by the implements of offering [and] by sacrificial butter.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first pāda is apparently addressed to the earth, differently from the others. Ppp. puts the verse before our vs. 22, and reads in c kumbhīr vedyāṁ saṁ carantāṁ . One or two of our mss. (Bs.O.) read uṣā́ in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: जनित्रीव प्रति हर्यासि सूनुं सं त्वा दधामि पृथिवीं पृथिव्या। उखा कुम्भी वेद्यां मा व्यथिष्ठा यज्ञायुधैराज्येनातिषक्ता ॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒ग्निः पच॑न्रक्षतु त्वा पु॒रस्ता॒दिन्द्रो॑ रक्षतु दक्षिण॒तो म॒रुत्वा॑न्। वरु॑णस्त्वा दृंहाद्ध॒रुणे॑ प्र॒तीच्या॑ उत्त॒रात्त्वा॒ सोमः॒ सं द॑दातै ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let Agni, cooking, defend thee on the east; let Indra, with the Maruts, defend on the south; may Varuṇa fix thee in the maintenance ( dharúṇa ) of the western [quarter]; on the north may Soma give thee together.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. corrects the meter of b by reading rakṣāt; and that of d by having varuṇas instead of somas . The verse is irregular, but by no means a jagatī . ⌊If we make varuṇas and somas exchange places, as suggested by Ppp., and read rakṣāt with Ppp., the vs. becomes a good triṣṭubh.⌋ In Kāuç. 61. 32 it is used when arranging the fire about the kettle.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अग्निः पचन्रक्षतु त्वा पुरस्तादिन्द्रो रक्षतु दक्षिणतो मरुत्वान्। वरुणस्त्वा दृंहाद्धरुणे प्रतीच्या उत्तरात्त्वा सोमः सं ददातै ॥

items.samhita_patha: पू॒ताः प॒वित्रैः॑ पवन्ते अ॒भ्राद्दिवं॑ च॒ यन्ति॑ पृथि॒वीं च॑ लो॒कान्। ता जी॑व॒ला जी॒वध॑न्याः प्रति॒ष्ठाः पात्र॒ आसि॑क्ताः॒ पर्य॒ग्निरि॑न्धाम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Purified with purifiers, they purify themselves from the cloud; they go both to heaven and to earth [as their] worlds; them, lively, rich in life, firm-standing, poured into the vessel ( pā́tra ), let the fire kindle about.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. puts the verse after our vs. 26, and reads at end of b dharmaṇā (cf. RV. x. 16. 3 b ), and in c, d jīvadhānyāt sametā ⌊cf. vs. 4⌋ pātrā ”siktāt . The verse is defective by a syllable in a , but the Anukr. passes this without notice. Kāuç. 61. 34 quotes the verse to accompany putting into the strainer.

items.samhita_patha_plain: पूताः पवित्रैः पवन्ते अभ्राद्दिवं च यन्ति पृथिवीं च लोकान्। ता जीवला जीवधन्याः प्रतिष्ठाः पात्र आसिक्ताः पर्यग्निरिन्धाम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: आ य॑न्ति दि॒वः पृ॑थि॒वीं स॑चन्ते॒ भूम्याः॑ सचन्ते॒ अध्य॒न्तरि॑क्षम्। शु॒द्धाः स॒तीस्ता उ॑ शुम्भन्त ए॒व ता नः॑ स्व॒र्गम॒भि लो॒कं न॑यन्तु ॥

commentaries.whitney: They come from the sky, they fasten on ( sac ) the earth; from the earth they fasten upon the atmosphere; being cleansed, they just cleanse themselves; let them conduct us to the heavenly world.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The accent of çúmbhante in c is unmotived. Ppp. reads ⌊cf. vss. 13 and 21 and note to vi. 115. 3⌋ çundhanti , which (or çumbhanti ) is decidedly preferable. That the reading in a is diváḥ p- is noted in the comm. to Prāt. ii. 68.

items.samhita_patha_plain: आ यन्ति दिवः पृथिवीं सचन्ते भूम्याः सचन्ते अध्यन्तरिक्षम्। शुद्धाः सतीस्ता उ शुम्भन्त एव ता नः स्वर्गमभि लोकं नयन्तु ॥

commentaries.whitney: Both as it were prevailing ( prabhú ) and also commensurate, also bright and clean, immortal—as such do ye, O waters, directed, helping, cook the rich-dish for the two spouses, ye of good refuge.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies in d emendation of āpaḥ॰çíkṣantīḥ to ā́paḥ çíkṣ- , the former seeming wholly unacceptable. Ppp. combines and reads praçiṣṭā ”pas sīkṣ- . Our text reads with the mss.

items.samhita_patha_plain: उतेव प्रभ्वीरुत संमितास उत शुक्राः शुचयश्चामृतासः। ता ओदनं दंपतिभ्यां प्रशिष्टा आपः शिक्षन्तीः पचता सुनाथाः ॥

commentaries.whitney: The numbered drops ( stoká ) fasten on the earth, being commensurate with breaths-and-expirations, with herbs; being scattered on, unnumbered, of good color, the clean ones have obtained all cleanness.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse, as noted above, is wanting in Ppp. It is quoted in Kāuç. 61. 36 to accompany the scattering in of the rice-grains after washing.

items.samhita_patha_plain: संख्याता स्तोकाः पृथिवीं सचन्ते प्राणापानैः संमिता ओषधीभिः। असंख्याता ओप्यमानाः सुवर्णाः सर्वं व्या᳡पुः शुचयः शुचित्वम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: उद्यो॑धन्त्य॒भि व॑ल्गन्ति त॒प्ताः फेन॑मस्यन्ति बहु॒लांश्च॑ बि॒न्दून्। योषे॑व दृ॒ष्ट्वा पति॒मृत्वि॑यायै॒तैस्त॑ण्डु॒लैर्भ॑वता॒ समा॑पः ॥

commentaries.whitney: They struggle up ( ud-yudh ), they dance on, being heated; they hurl foam and abundant drops ( bindú ); like a woman that is in her season, seeing her husband, unite yourselves, O waters, with these rice-grains.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation assumes the emendation, made in our edited text, of ṛ́tviyā yā́ , for the ṛ́tviyāya of all the mss. ⌊See SPP's note on this matter, p. 231. He says ṛtviya = māithuna . Ppp. reads ṛtviyāvāis tāis taṇḍ- . In Kāuç. 61. 37 the verse accompanies the making of the water to boil.

commentaries.whitney: Make thou them stand up, as they sit on the bottom; let them touch themselves all over with the waters; I have measured with vessels ( pā́tra ) the water that is here; measured are the rice-grains that are these directions.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last pāda is translated as if yádīmā́ḥ (p. yádi imā́ḥ ) were meant as equivalent to yád imā́ḥ , corresponding to the yád etát of c . Ppp. has sṛjantām at end of b . ⌊Here, at the end of a decad-division, ends the twenty-sixth prapāṭhaka .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: उत्थापय सीदतो बुध्न एनानद्भिरात्मानमभि सं स्पृशन्ताम्। अमासि पात्रैरुदकं यदेतन्मितास्तण्डुलाः प्रदिशो यदीमाः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Reach thou forth the sickle ( párçu ), hasten, take [it] quickly; let them, not harming, cut ( dā ) the herbs at the joint; they of whom Soma compassed the kingship—let the plants be without wrath toward us.
commentaries.whitney_notes: One or two of our mss. read in a páraçum (M.W.; O. párárçum ); and, as usual, some (O.D.R.) accent rā́jyam in c . Ppp. has harantu for harāu ’ṣam in a ; and, in c , soma yāsām . Amanyutāḥ is undivided in the pada -text. In Kāuç. 61. 38 the first pāda is used with handing over the sickle for gathering the darbha -grass; the second pāda,* in 61. 39, with cutting it above the joints; and in 1. 24, 25 both for a similar purpose; so also the first pāda (or the verse) in 8. 11; and yet again both in the comm. to 137. 4. *⌊Quoted as oṣadhīr dāntu parvan at i. 25 and 61. 39. According to Daç. Kar. (note to 137. 4), the quotation pra yacha parçum covers a pāda and a half, that is, it includes the ahiṅsantas which is omitted in the quotation of b .⌋

items.samhita_patha: नवं॑ ब॒र्हिरो॑द॒नाय॑ स्तृणीत प्रि॒यं हृ॒दश्चक्षु॑षो व॒ल्ग्व᳡स्तु। तस्मि॑न्दे॒वाः स॒ह दै॒वीर्वि॑शन्त्वि॒मं प्राश्न॑न्त्वृ॒तुभि॑र्नि॒षद्य॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Strew ye a new barhís for the rice-dish; be it dear to the heart, agreeable to the eye; on it let the gods [and] the divine ones (f.) settle ( viç ) together; sitting down ( ni-sad ), let them partake of this with the seasons.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The mss. read in b priyā́m , but our text makes the unavoidable emendation to -yám . Some of the mss. also are bothered over the unusual combination lgva in b : ⌊thus Bs. has vaglàv astu; R. valgáv astu; T. valgvustu . And again, in d , Bs. reads -çnan ṛ́t- , and O.s.m.R. -çnanty ṛt- . The verse accompanies in Kāuç. 61. 40 the strewing of the barhis .

items.samhita_patha_plain: नवं बर्हिरोदनाय स्तृणीत प्रियं हृदश्चक्षुषो वल्ग्व᳡स्तु। तस्मिन्देवाः सह दैवीर्विशन्त्विमं प्राश्नन्त्वृतुभिर्निषद्य ॥

commentaries.whitney: O forest tree, sit on the strewn barhís , being commensurate with the Agni-praises ( agniṣṭomá ), with the deities; like a form well made by an artisan ( tváṣṭṛ ) with a knife, so ( enā́ ) let the eager ones be seen round about in the vessel ( pā́tra ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Bp. and Bs.s.m. read svádhiyā at end of c . The anomalous hiatus enā́ (p. enā́ ) ehā́ḥ is noted in Prāt. iii. 34. Ppp. reads svadhityāināhyāṣ pari pātre dadṛçyām , which is welcome as ridding us of the wholly unsupported form dadṛçrām; ⌊cf. Gram. §813⌋. In Kāuç. 61. 43, the verse accompanies the setting of a vessel ( pātrī ) upon the barhis; in Vāit. 10. 7, the laying of the sacrificial post upon the same (the editor of Kāuç. regards it as quoted also in 15. 11, but the verse there intended must be rather vi. 125. 1).

commentaries.whitney: In sixty autumns may he (?) seek unto the treasure-keepers; may he attain unto the sky with the cooked [offering]; may both fathers [and] sons live upon him; make thou this one to go unto the heaven-going end of the fire.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last pāda admits of various other constructions. Both here and in vs. 41 (where pāda a is repeated) Bp. reads at the beginning çaṣṭhyā́m . In c , O.p.m.R. accent jīvā́n . Ppp. puts the verse after our vs. 35, and reads, for a , ṣaṣṭyām çaradbhyaṣ paridadhma enam; for c , upāi ’naṁ putrān pitaraç ca sīdām; in d , imam for etam . There is no reason why the Anukr. should regard the verse as anything but a regular triṣṭubh . In Kāuç. 62. 9 it accompanies the setting down of the rice-dish westward from the fire.

commentaries.whitney: A maintainer, maintain thyself in the maintenance of the earth; thee that art unmoved let the deities make to move ( cyu ); thee shall the two spouses, living, having living sons, cause to remove ( ud-vas ) out of the fire-holder.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines -vyā ’cyutam in a-b , omits the meter-disturbing (and probably intrusive) tvā of c , reads in c -putrā , and in d ud vāsayāthaṣ p- . The Anukr. takes no notice of the redundant syllable in our c . In Kāuç. 61. 41, the verse accompanies the removal of the vessel; in Vāit. 10. 9, the insertion of the end of the sacrificial post in the ground.

commentaries.whitney: Thou hast come together unto all the worlds, having conquered; however many [be] the desires, thou hast made them wholly satisfied; plunge ye (du.) in—both the stirring-stick [and] the spoon; take thou him up upon one vessel.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This obscure verse wins no light from Kāuç. (62. 1), which says simply iti mantroktam , connecting it with xi. 1. 24. Some of our mss. (P.M.W.T.) read abhí for ádhi in d . We should expect in c gāhetām , as the nouns are not vocative. Ppp. reads in a samāgān abhicikya , and in b kāmān samitāu purastāt . ⌊See p. lxxxviii.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Strew thou on, spread forward, smear over with ghee this vessel; as a lowing cow ( usrā́ ) [toward] a young [calf] desiring the teat, do ye, O gods, utter the sound hing toward this one.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Strew on': i.e., specifically, make an upastaraṇa or covering of butter. In Ppp. the second half-verse is wholly corrupt The verse is quoted in Kāuç. 61. 45, as accompanying the operation described, and the next verse is added in 61. 46 when the operation is completed.

items.samhita_patha_plain: उप स्तृणीहि प्रथय पुरस्ताद्घृतेन पात्रमभि घारयैतत्। वाश्रेवोस्रा तरुणं स्तनस्युमिमं देवासो अभिहिङ्कृणोत ॥

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. begins with apāskārāir , and makes çrayātāi and suparṇas change places in c .

commentaries.whitney_notes: Kāuç. 62. 11 quotes the verse ( iti mantroktam ), but casts no light upon it. ⌊Has a second pácati fallen out after jāye? ⌋

commentaries.whitney: How many of her fasten on ( sac ) the earth, what sons came forth into being from us (pl.)—all those do ye (du.) call to you in the vessel;. knowing the navel, the young ones ( çíçu ) shall come together.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The mss. (excepting R.D.) leave sacante in a unaccented. Ppp. reads after it ‘smat . The verse, especially the first pāda, is obscure. 'Navel' = 'central point, place of union.' The Anukr. does not heed the deficiency of a syllable in c ; it means us, perhaps, to resolve ta-ā́n .

items.samhita_patha: वसो॒र्या धारा॒ मधु॑ना॒ प्रपी॑ना घृ॒तेन॑ मि॒श्रा अ॒मृत॑स्य॒ नाभ॑यः। सर्वा॒स्ता अव॑ रुन्धे स्व॒र्गः ष॒ष्ट्यां श॒रत्सु॑ निधि॒पा अ॒भी᳡च्छा॑त् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What streams ( dhā́rā ) of good ( vásu ) [there are], fattened with honey, mixed with ghee, navels of immortality—all those doth the heaven-goer (? svargá ) take possession of; in sixty autumns may he seek unto the treasure-keepers.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last and obscurest pāda is identical with 34 a . The Anukr. perhaps accepts the redundant syllable of b and the deficient of c as balancing each other. The verse is used, with 44 below, in Kāuç. 62. 18, to accompany the further pouring in of juices. Ppp. reads samaktās for prapīnās in a , and dhāmayas at end of b , and combines -pā ’bh- in d .

commentaries.whitney: He shall seek unto it, [as] treasure-keepers unto a treasure; let those who are others be not lords ( ánīçvara ) about; given by us, deposited, heaven-going, with three divisions it has ascended to three heavens ( svargá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. again combines in a -pā ’bhy . Kāuç. 62. 10 makes the verse accompany the division of the rice-dish into three parts. There is no reason for calling it bhurij , as the Anukr. does.

commentaries.whitney: Let Agni burn the demon that is godless; let the flesh-eating piçācá not have a draught here; we thrust him, we bar him away from us; let the Ādityas, the An̄girases, fasten on him.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Doubtless we should emend to rundhmas in c . Ppp. reads in d ādityā no an̄g- , thus rectifying the meter. The Anukr. notices this time the redundance of the pāda. Doubtless, as often elsewhere, we are to contract to ādityāí ’nam . In Kāuç. 62. 14 the verse is made to accompany the carrying of fire around the offering. ⌊BR. render the force of pra by defining pra-pā as 'sich an's Trinken machen.'⌋

commentaries.whitney: To the Ādityas, the An̄girases, I announce this honey mingled with ghee; with cleansed hands, not smiting down [anything of] the Brahman's, go ye (du.), O well-doers, unto this heavenly world ( svargá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The description by the Anukr. is quite wrong. The use by Kāuç. 62. 18 was noted above, under vs. 41 . ⌊For the use of the genitive, W. has noted a reference to Delbrück's Altindische Syntax , p. 161.⌋

commentaries.whitney: I have obtained this highest division of it, from which world the most exalted one obtained [it] completely; pour thou on the butter ( sarpís ); anoint with ghee; this is the portion of our An̄giras here.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has in a a different order of words: idaṁ kāṇḍam uttamaṁ prāpam asya . The verse (with xi. 1. 31: the first half of each) is quoted in Kāuç. 62. 15, and again (the second half of each) in 62. 17, in connection with anointing the vessel with butter.

commentaries.whitney: Unto truth, unto penance, and unto the deities, we deliver this deposit ( nidhí ), [this] treasure ( çevadhí ); let it not be lost ( ava-gā ) in our play, nor in the meeting; do not ye release it to another in preference to ( purā́ ) me.
commentaries.whitney_notes: One or two of our mss. (R.D.) accent at the end mát; and the word is not found without accent unless here and at xi. 4. 26. ⌊SPP. reads mát with 8 of his authorities, against 7 that have mat .⌋ Ppp. reads in b dadhmas . This and the two following verses are quoted, with a number of others, in Kāuç. 68. 27, at a later point in the rice-dish ceremony. ⌊With c , cf. 52 a .⌋

commentaries.whitney: I cook; I give; verily upon my action [and] deed (? karúṇa ) the wife; a virgin (? kāúmāra ) world hath been born, a son; take ye (du.) hold after vigor ( váyas ) that hath what is superior.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation here is purely mechanical. Ppp. puts the verse after our vs. 48, and reads in a , for dadāmi , ud vadāmi ⌊thus suggesting the probably correct restoration of the pāda ( aham u dadādmi )⌋, and in c putrās . The verse (10 + 11: 11 + 11 = 43) is very ill described by the Anukr.

commentaries.whitney: No offense is here, nor support (? ādhārá ), nor that one goes agreeing ( sam-am ) with friends; this vessel of ours is set down not empty; the cooked [dish] shall enter again him that cooked it.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse is little more intelligible than the preceding. Ppp. puts c after d , and reads at the end of c astu instead of etat . ⌊It is hardly worth while to discuss the accent of ásti .⌋

commentaries.whitney: May we do what is dear to them that are dear; whosoever hate [us], let them go to darkness; milch-cow, draft-ox, each coming vigor ( váyas )—let them thrust away the death that comes from men.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Or, 'that concerns, comes upon, men' ( pāúruṣeya ). The Anukr. seems to accept the two redundant syllables of c ( evá an intrusion) as compensating for the deficiency in a . According to Kāuç. 62. 19, the verse is used of 'the milch-cow etc.' north of the fire.

commentaries.whitney: The fires ire in concord, one with another—he that fastens on the herbs, and he that [fastens on] the rivers; as many gods as send heat ( ā-tap ) in the sky—gold hath become the light of him that cooks.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads sindhum in b , and dadhatu * (for pacatas ) in d . In Kāuç. 62. 22, the verse (with xi. 1. 28) is made to accompany the laying on of a piece of gold; it is also quoted in 68. 27, with vss. 46-48, etc.: see note to vs. 46. The Anukr. does not notice the lack of a syllable in a . *⌊Intending dadhato? ⌋

commentaries.whitney: This one of skins ( tvác ) hath come into being on man; not naked are all the animals ( paçú ) that are other; ye (du.) cause to wrap ( paridhā ) yourselves ( ātmán ) with authority ( kṣatrá ), a home-woven garment, the mouth of the rice-dish.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation is as literal as possible; but other constructions may be made in the second half-verse. Ppp. leaves the hiatus between a and b , babhūva an- ; it combines -gnās sarve in b ; and it reads in c dhāpayeta , with a division-line after it. Kāuç. 62. 23 makes the verse accompany the depositing of such a garment, with gold. ⌊Has the vs. anything to do with the legend, cited under ii. 13. 3, about the cow and her skin, which the gods took from man and gave to the cow?⌋

commentaries.whitney: What [untruth] thou shalt speak at the dice, what at the meeting, or what untruth thou shalt speak from desire of gain—clothing yourselves (du.) in the same web ( tántu ), ye shall settle in it all pollution.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. rectifies the meter of a by reading vadasi; in b it has dhane instead of vadās; in c it gives saha for abhi . The Anukr. does not notice the deficiency in a . The verse is quoted in Kāuç. 63. 1 (next after vs. 51), with the explanation 'the two become dressed in the same garment.' ⌊With a , cf. 46 c .⌋

commentaries.whitney: Win thou rain; go unto the gods; thou shalt make smoke fly up out of the skin; about to become all-expanded, ghee-backed, go thou, of like origin, unto that world.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The second half-verse is identical with 19 a, b above. Ppp. begins b with tatas instead of tvacas; and it has a different second half: viçvavyacā viçvakarmā svargas sayoniṁ lokam upa yāhy ekam , which seems less unintelligible. In Kāuç. 63. 5 the verse is quoted (together with xi. 1. 28 b ) with the direction 'he draws off [the garment?].'

items.samhita_patha_plain: वर्षं वनुष्वापि गच्छ देवांस्त्वचो धूमं पर्युत्पातयासि। विश्वव्यचा घृतपृष्ठो भविष्यन्त्सयोनिर्लोकमुप याह्येतम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: त॒न्वं᳡ स्व॒र्गो ब॑हु॒धा वि च॑क्रे॒ यथा॑ वि॒द आ॒त्मन्न॒न्यव॑र्णाम्। अपा॑जैत्कृ॒ष्णां रुश॑तीं पुना॒नो या लोहि॑नी॒ तां ते॑ अ॒ग्नौ जु॑होमि ॥

commentaries.whitney: The heaven-goer hath variously changed his body, as he finds (? vidé ) in himself one of another color; he hath conquered off the black one, purifying a shining one ( rúçat ); the one that is red, that I offer ( hu ) to thee in the fire.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The adjectives here are all fem., relating to 'body' ( tanū́ ). The defective meter of b helps to make the isolated ⌊or rather, unusual?⌋ vidé ⌊see Gram. §613⌋ suspicious; the Anukr. takes no notice of the deficiency. The first half-verse is corrupt in Ppp., so that the comparison gives us no help. In Kāuç. 63. 8 the verse accompanies the scattering on of other husks ( phalīkaraṇān ). ⌊For the form ajāit , see the references under vi. 32. 2.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: तन्वं᳡ स्वर्गो बहुधा वि चक्रे यथा विद आत्मन्नन्यवर्णाम्। अपाजैत्कृष्णां रुशतीं पुनानो या लोहिनी तां ते अग्नौ जुहोमि ॥

commentaries.whitney: To the eastern quarter, to Agni as overlord, to the black [serpent] as defender, to Āditya having arrows, we commit thee here; guard ye him for us until our coming; may he lead on our appointed [life-time] here unto old age; let old age commit us unto death; then may we be united with the cooked [offering].

commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Here ends the third anuvāka , with 1 hymn and 60 verses. The quoted Anukr. says svargaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ , i.e., 'the svarga [-hymn] is sixty.' The stem svarga , in one form or another, occurs a dozen times in the hymn.⌋

items.samhita_patha: ददा॒मीत्ये॒व ब्रू॑या॒दनु॑ चैना॒मभु॑त्सत। व॒शां ब्र॒ह्मभ्यो॒ याच॑द्भ्य॒स्तत्प्र॒जाव॒दप॑त्यवत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: I give [her]—thus should he say, if they have noticed (? anu-budh ) her—[I give] the cow ( vaçā́ ) to the priests ( brahmán ) that ask for her; that brings progeny, descendants.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Perhaps ánu ábhutsata is rather 'have recognized': i.e., have made her out to be the kind of cow that is called vaçā́; or there may be in it something of the meaning of anu-jnā: 'have approved, or taken a liking to.' ⌊Cf. MGS. i. 8. 6 and p. 150.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: ददामीत्येव ब्रूयादनु चैनामभुत्सत। वशां ब्रह्मभ्यो याचद्भ्यस्तत्प्रजावदपत्यवत् ॥

items.samhita_patha: प्र॒जया॒ स वि क्री॑णीते प॒शुभि॒श्चोप॑ दस्यति। य आ॑र्षे॒येभ्यो॒ याच॑द्भ्यो दे॒वानां॒ गां न दित्स॑ति ॥

commentaries.whitney: He bargains away his progeny and becomes exhausted of cattle who is not willing to give the cow ( gó ) of the gods to the sons of seers that ask for her.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Pādas c, d recur as 12 a, b .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: प्रजया स वि क्रीणीते पशुभिश्चोप दस्यति। य आर्षेयेभ्यो याचद्भ्यो देवानां गां न दित्सति ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: प्रऽजया । स: । वि । क्रीणीते । पशुऽभि: । च । उप । दस्यति । य: । आर्षेयेभ्य: । याचत्ऽभ्य: । देवानाम् । गाम् । न । दित्सति ॥४.२॥

items.samhita_patha: कू॒टया॑स्य॒ सं शी॑र्यन्ते श्लो॒णया॑ का॒टम॑र्दति। ब॒ण्डया॑ दह्यन्ते गृ॒हाः का॒णया॑ दीयते॒ स्वम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: By a hornless one they are crushed for him; by a lame one he falls (? ard ) into a pit; by a crippled one his houses are burned; by a one-eyed one his possessions are taken away (?).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The adjectives are feminine, and the sense doubtless is that as the result of giving such defective cows the thing threatened will happen. In a , probably the subject to be understood is gṛhā́s , as in c ; b and c have perhaps become transposed—and, in that case, svám might be the subject also of árdati . ⌊Ppp. has kāṭam , like the Vulgate.⌋ The translation of d implies emendation (which seems advisable ⌊cf. W. in AJP. xiii. 302⌋) of kāṇáyā to kāṇáyā́: i.e. kāṇáyā: ā́: dīyate . Ppp. has jīyate 'is harmed,' which would remove the difficulty. ⌊On kūṭá , see von Bradke, KZ. xxxiv. 157.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: कूटयास्य सं शीर्यन्ते श्लोणया काटमर्दति। बण्डया दह्यन्ते गृहाः काणया दीयते स्वम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: कूटया । अस्य । सम् । शीर्यन्ते । श्लोणया । काटम् । अर्दति । बण्डया । दह्यन्ते । गृहा: । काणया । दीयते । स्वम् ॥४.३॥

items.samhita_patha: वि॑लोहि॒तो अ॑धि॒ष्ठाना॑च्छ॒क्नो वि॑न्दति॒ गोप॑तिम्। तथा॑ व॒शायाः॒ संवि॑द्यं दुरद॒भ्ना ह्यु१॒॑च्यसे॑ ॥
items.pada_patha: वि॒ऽलो॒हि॒त: । अ॒धि॒ऽस्थाना॑त् । श॒क्न: । वि॒न्द॒ति॒ । गोऽप॑तिम् । तथा॑ । व॒शाया॑: । सम्ऽवि॑द्यम् । दु॒र॒द॒भ्ना । हि ।॒ उ॒च्यसे॑ ॥४.४॥

commentaries.whitney: Anæmia ( vilohitá ) from the station of the dung visits ( vid ) the master of kine; so is the agreement (?) of the cow; for door-damaging (?) art thou called.
commentaries.whitney_notes: [ Kaçyapa.—tripañcāçat. mantroktavaçādevatyam. ānuṣṭubham: 7. bhurij; 20. virāj; 32. uṣṇigbṛhatīgarbhā; 42. bṛhatīgarbhā. ] Found also in Pāipp. xvii. (with slight differences of verse-order ⌊4, 6, 5, 8, 7, 9 and 17, 19, 18, 20⌋). Not noticed at all in Vāit., and in Kāuç. only once, in 66. 20, where, with x. 10, it (or the first verse) is to be spoken by the giver of a cow, after sprinkling etc. Translated; Ludwig, p. 448; Henry, 203, 248; Griffith, ii. 120; Bloomfield, 174, 656. Nearly everything in the second half-verse is doubtful. The majority of our mss. read sáṁvidyam (p. sám॰vidyam ), but sā́ṁ- instead is given by M.s.m.O.s.m. and D.; and in R. sā́ṁ- is emended to sāṁ- . Sā́ṁvidya seems a much more probable form of stem. The Pet. Lexx. render 'possession,' which is very unsatisfactory. Duradabhnā́ (also in vs. 19) seems pretty clearly the reading of nearly all our mss. in c , though it might, as usual in such cases, be -bhrā́ in most; Bp. has (both times) apparently -bhdnā , and O. ⌊in vs. 4⌋ -bdnā or -b-h-nā (the b and h separate letters, as again below in xiii. 1. 25 c ). The word is not divided in the pada -text. The translation given is ⌊suggested by⌋ that of the Pet. Lexx.; Ludwig renders here 'unbetrieglich' (undeceivable), but leaves the word untranslated in vs. 19. The second person ucyáse is quite unexpected; ⌊most of our⌋ saṁhitā -mss. read hy ū̀3cyáse; ⌊and SPP's are much at variance⌋. ⌊As alternative rendering in a, b , W. notes 'from standing on her dung.'⌋ Ppp. reads, in c, d , svāṁ vidyuṁ duritagrāhy uccase .

items.samhita_patha_plain: विलोहितो अधिष्ठानाच्छक्नो विन्दति गोपतिम्। तथा वशायाः संविद्यं दुरदभ्ना ह्यु१च्यसे ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: विऽलोहित: । अधिऽस्थानात् । शक्न: । विन्दति । गोऽपतिम् । तथा । वशाया: । सम्ऽविद्यम् । दुरदभ्ना । हि । उच्यसे ॥४.४॥

items.samhita_patha: प॒दोर॑स्या अधि॒ष्ठाना॑द्वि॒क्लिन्दु॒र्नाम॑ विन्दति। अ॑नाम॒नात्सं शी॑र्यन्ते॒ या मुखे॑नोप॒जिघ्र॑ति ॥

commentaries.whitney: From the station of the two feet of her, soaking (? viklíndu ) namely visits [him]; unexpectedly (?) are they crushed who snuff at her with the mouth.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Here, too, much is obscure and doubtful. The first part might be: 'From the station of her ⌊or 'from standing on her,' as W. queries⌋, soaking of the feet visits ⌊him⌋,' as it is hard to see what two feet have to do with a cow. And in d yā́s can be either subject or object, and jíghrati either sing, or pl. I take anāmanā́t from root man; Ludwig renders it 'without becoming ill'; the Pet. Lexx. explain the word as meaning a kind of disease. Ppp. reads, in a, b , asyā ’dhiṣṭhānād vikulaṁ dvin nāma .

items.samhita_patha_plain: पदोरस्या अधिष्ठानाद्विक्लिन्दुर्नाम विन्दति। अनामनात्सं शीर्यन्ते या मुखेनोपजिघ्रति ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: पदो: । अस्या: । अधिऽस्थानात् । विऽक्लिन्दु: । नाम । विन्दति । अनामनात् । सम् । शीर्यन्ते । या: । मुखेन । उपऽजिघ्रति ॥४.५॥

items.samhita_patha: यो अ॑स्याः॒ कर्णा॑वास्कु॒नोत्या स दे॒वेषु॑ वृश्चते। लक्ष्म॑ कुर्व॒ इति॒ मन्य॑ते॒ कनी॑यः कृणुते॒ स्वम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whoever punches ( ā-sku ) the two ears of her, he falls under the wrath of the gods; if he thinks "I am making a mark," he makes his possessions less.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यो अस्याः कर्णावास्कुनोत्या स देवेषु वृश्चते। लक्ष्म कुर्व इति मन्यते कनीयः कृणुते स्वम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: य: । अस्या: । कर्णौ । आऽस्कुनोति । आ । स: । देवेषु । वृश्चते । लक्ष्म । कुर्वे । इति । मन्यते । कनीय: । कृणुते । स्वम् ॥४.६॥

items.samhita_patha: यद॑स्याः॒ कस्मै॑ चि॒द्भोगा॑य॒ बाला॒न्कश्चि॑त्प्रकृ॒न्तति॑। ततः॑ किशो॒रा म्रि॑यन्ते व॒त्सांश्च॒ घातु॑को॒ वृकः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: If, for any one's advantage, any one cuts off the tail-tuft of her, then his colts die, and the wolf slays his calves.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Or (in a ), 'for any advantage or use.' Ppp. makes 7 c, d and 8 c, d change places. It reads also vālān in b .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदस्याः कस्मै चिद्भोगाय बालान्कश्चित्प्रकृन्तति। ततः किशोरा म्रियन्ते वत्सांश्च घातुको वृकः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यत्। अस्या: । कस्मै । चित् । भोगाय । बालान् । क: । चित् । प्रऽकृन्तति । तत: । किशोरा: । म्रियन्ते । वत्सान्। च । घातुक: । वृक: ॥४.७॥

items.samhita_patha: यद॑स्या॒ गोप॑तौ स॒त्या लोम॒ ध्वाङ्क्षो॒ अजी॑हिडत्। ततः॑ कुमा॒रा म्रि॑यन्ते॒ यक्ष्मो॑ विन्दत्यनाम॒नात् ॥

commentaries.whitney: If of her, while being with her master, a crow hath vexed ( hīḍ ) the hair, then his boys die, [and] the yákṣma visits him unexpectedly (?).
commentaries.whitney_notes: As to anāmanā́t , see note to vs. 5. The first pāda apparendy means 'in presence of her master,' and so, 'without his interference for her protection.' ⌊Ppp. combines tataṣ k- in c .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदस्या गोपतौ सत्या लोम ध्वाङ्क्षो अजीहिडत्। ततः कुमारा म्रियन्ते यक्ष्मो विन्दत्यनामनात् ॥

items.samhita_patha: यद॑स्याः॒ पल्पू॑लनं॒ शकृ॑द्दा॒सी स॒मस्य॑ति। ततोऽप॑रूपं जायते॒ तस्मा॒दव्ये॑ष्य॒देन॑सः ॥
items.pada_patha: यत् । अ॒स्या॒: । पल्पू॑लनम् । शकृ॑त् । दा॒सी । स॒म्ऽअस्य॑ति । तत॑: । अप॑ऽरूपम् । जा॒य॒ते॒ । तस्मा॑त् । अवि॑ऽएष्यत् । एन॑स: ॥४.९॥

commentaries.whitney: If the lye, the dung of her a barbarian woman flings together, then is born what is deformed, what will not escape from that sin.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All our mss. appear to read distinctly palpūl- in a , yet they are never to be trusted to make the distinction between lp and ly . Apparently the word is used here for 'urine,' and the meaning is 'if such precious stuff is carelessly treated by a slave-woman ( dāsī ).' Ppp. reads ‘pirūpaṁ in c . We have to resolve as-i-āḥ to fill out the meter of a .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदस्याः पल्पूलनं शकृद्दासी समस्यति। ततोऽपरूपं जायते तस्मादव्येष्यदेनसः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यत् । अस्या: । पल्पूलनम् । शकृत् । दासी । सम्ऽअस्यति । तत: । अपऽरूपम् । जायते । तस्मात् । अविऽएष्यत् । एनस: ॥४.९॥

items.samhita_patha: जाय॑माना॒भि जा॑यते दे॒वान्त्सब्रा॑ह्मणान्व॒शा। तस्मा॑द्ब्र॒ह्मभ्यो॒ देयै॒षा तदा॑हुः॒ स्वस्य॒ गोप॑नम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: When being born, the cow ( vaçā́ ) is born for ( abhí ) the gods together with the Brahmans; therefore she is to be given to the priests ( brahmán ); that people call the guarding ( gópana ) of one's possessions.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text makes the extraordinary division gó॰panam ⌊for the sake of the play upon go 'cow'?⌋, as if the word were not a simple derivative from root gup! 'For' ( abhí ): more literally 'unto, into the possession of.'

items.samhita_patha_plain: जायमानाभि जायते देवान्त्सब्राह्मणान्वशा। तस्माद्ब्रह्मभ्यो देयैषा तदाहुः स्वस्य गोपनम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: जायमाना: । अभि । जायते । देवान् । सऽब्राह्मणान् । वशा । तस्मात् । ब्रह्मऽभ्य: । देया । एषा । तत् । आहु: । स्वस्य । गोपनम् ॥४.१०॥

items.samhita_patha: य ए॑नां व॒निमा॒यन्ति॒ तेषां॑ दे॒वकृ॑ता व॒शा। ब्र॑ह्म॒ज्येयं॒ तद॑ब्रुव॒न्य ए॑नां निप्रिया॒यते॑ ॥
items.pada_patha: ये । ए॒ना॒म् । व॒निम् । आ॒ऽयन्ति॑ । तेषा॑म् । दे॒वऽकृ॑ता । व॒शा । ब्र॒ह्म॒ऽज्येय॑म् । तत् । अ॒ब्रु॒व॒न् । य: । ए॒ना॒म् । नि॒ऽप्रि॒य॒यते॑ ॥४.११॥

commentaries.whitney: They who come to the winning ( vaní ) of her, theirs is the god-made cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋; they called it bráhman -scathing, if anyone keeps her to himself.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Pāda b seems to mean virtually 'she is by the gods made theirs.' Ppp. reads at the end (as also in vss. 21, 25) nu priyāyate , and nipr- is certainly very questionable, since no nipriya nor even root prī + ni occurs. The minor Pet Lex. gives the word two totally different explanations, under nipriyāy and priyāy respectively.

items.samhita_patha_plain: य एनां वनिमायन्ति तेषां देवकृता वशा। ब्रह्मज्येयं तदब्रुवन्य एनां निप्रियायते ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: ये । एनाम् । वनिम् । आऽयन्ति । तेषाम् । देवऽकृता । वशा । ब्रह्मऽज्येयम् । तत् । अब्रुवन् । य: । एनाम् । निऽप्रिययते ॥४.११॥

items.samhita_patha: य आ॑र्षे॒येभ्यो॒ याच॑द्भ्यो दे॒वानां॒ गां न दित्स॑ति। आ स दे॒वेषु॑ वृश्चते ब्राह्म॒णानां॑ च म॒न्यवे॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whoever is not willing to give the cow ( gó ) of the gods to the sons of seers that ask for her, he falls under the wrath of the gods and the fury of the Brahmans.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for a, b , ya enāṁ yācadbhya ārṣeyebhyo nirucchati . ⌊We had a, b above as 2 c, d , and c as 6 b .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: य आर्षेयेभ्यो याचद्भ्यो देवानां गां न दित्सति। आ स देवेषु वृश्चते ब्राह्मणानां च मन्यवे ॥

items.samhita_patha: यो अ॑स्य॒ स्याद्व॑शाभो॒गो अ॒न्यामि॑च्छेत॒ तर्हि॒ सः। हिंस्ते॒ अद॑त्ता॒ पुरु॑षं याचि॒तां च॒ न दित्स॑ति ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whatever may be his use for the cow ( vaçā́- ), he should then seek another [cow]; she, ungiven, harms a man, if he is not willing to give her when asked for.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has a quite different version of a-c : yasyā ’nya syād vaçābhogo ‘nyām icchetu barhiṣaḥ: hiṅsrā ṇi dhatsva gopatiṁ . We should expect pū́ruṣam at end of c , as elsewhere in such a position.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यो अस्य स्याद्वशाभोगो अन्यामिच्छेत तर्हि सः। हिंस्ते अदत्ता पुरुषं याचितां च न दित्सति ॥

items.samhita_patha: यथा॑ शेव॒धिर्निहि॑तो ब्राह्म॒णानां॒ तथा॑ व॒शा। तामे॒तद॒च्छाय॑न्ति॒ यस्मि॒न्कस्मिं॑श्च॒ जाय॑ते ॥

commentaries.whitney: As a deposited treasure ( çevadhí ), so of the Brahmans is the cow ( vaçā́ ); accordingly ⌊ etát ⌋ they come unto her, in whosesoever possession she is born.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यथा शेवधिर्निहितो ब्राह्मणानां तथा वशा। तामेतदच्छायन्ति यस्मिन्कस्मिंश्च जायते ॥

items.samhita_patha: स्वमे॒तद॑च्छायन्ति॒ यद्व॒शां ब्रा॑ह्म॒णा अ॒भि। यथै॑नान॒न्यस्मि॑ञ्जिनी॒यादे॒वास्या॑ नि॒रोध॑नम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: They come thus unto their own property, namely the Brahmans unto the cow; as one might scathe them in any other respect (?), so is the keeping back of her.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The third pāda is unclear, and the bad meter makes the reading suspicious; yet Ppp. has the same, and varies only in combining brāhmaṇā ’bhi in b , and combining and reading ’syā ’dhirohaṇaṁ in d . Most of our mss. (all except D. and R.s.ni.) have the false accent brā́hmaṇās in b ; our text emends. The Anukr. takes no notice of the redundant syllable in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: स्वमेतदच्छायन्ति यद्वशां ब्राह्मणा अभि। यथैनानन्यस्मिञ्जिनीयादेवास्या निरोधनम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: चरे॑दे॒वा त्रै॑हाय॒णादवि॑ज्ञातगदा स॒ती। व॒शां च॑ वि॒द्यान्ना॑रद ब्राह्म॒णास्तर्ह्ये॒ष्याः᳡ ॥
items.pada_patha: चरे॑त् । ए॒व । आ । त्रै॒हा॒य॒नात् । अवि॑ज्ञातऽगदा । स॒ती । व॒शाम् । च॒ । वि॒द्यात् । ना॒र॒द॒ । ब्रा॒ह्म॒णा: । तर्हि॑ । ए॒ष्या᳡: ॥४.१६॥

commentaries.whitney: She may go about until ⌊ ā́ ⌋ the space of three years, being of unrecognized ( vi-jñā ) speech ( -gada ); should he know the cow, O Nārada, then the Brahmans are to be sought.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This is obscure, but appears to mean that the cow may not betray herself as a vaçā for as much as three years; but, as soon as she is recognized as such, she must be delivered over to the Brahmans. The pada -text has in a , of course, evá: ā́: tr- .

items.samhita_patha_plain: चरेदेवा त्रैहायणादविज्ञातगदा सती। वशां च विद्यान्नारद ब्राह्मणास्तर्ह्येष्याः᳡ ॥

items.samhita_patha: य ए॑ना॒मव॑शा॒माह॑ दे॒वानां॒ निहि॑तं नि॒धिम्। उ॒भौ तस्मै॑ भवाश॒र्वौ प॑रि॒क्रम्येषु॑मस्यतः ॥
items.pada_patha: य: । ए॒ना॒म् । अव॑शाम् । आह॑ । दे॒वाना॑म् । निऽहि॑तम् । नि॒ऽधिम् । उ॒भौ । तस्मै॑ । भ॒वा॒श॒र्वौ । प॒रि॒ऽक्रम्य॑ । इषु॑म् । अ॒स्य॒त॒: ॥४.१७॥

commentaries.whitney: Whoever declares her to be not the cow, the deposited deposit of the gods, at him Bhava-and-Çarva, both, striding about, hurl the arrow.

items.samhita_patha_plain: य एनामवशामाह देवानां निहितं निधिम्। उभौ तस्मै भवाशर्वौ परिक्रम्येषुमस्यतः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: य: । एनाम् । अवशाम् । आह । देवानाम् । निऽहितम् । निऽधिम् । उभौ । तस्मै । भवाशर्वौ । परिऽक्रम्य । इषुम् । अस्यत: ॥४.१७॥

items.samhita_patha: यो अ॑स्या॒ ऊधो॒ न वे॒दाथो॑ अस्या॒ स्तना॑नु॒त। उ॒भये॑नै॒वास्मै॑ दुहे॒ दातुं॒ चेदश॑कद्व॒शाम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whoever knows not the udder of her, and likewise the teats of her, to him she yields milk with both, if he has been able to give the cow.
commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, probably, if her owner has sought no profit from her (cf. Ludwig). The first pāda is quoted under Prāt. ii. 52, as an example of ūdho (not ūdhar ) before a sonant. A number of our mss. read veda , without accent.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यो अस्या ऊधो न वेदाथो अस्या स्तनानुत। उभयेनैवास्मै दुहे दातुं चेदशकद्वशाम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: य: । अस्या: । ऊध: । न । वेद । अथो इति । अस्या: । स्तनान् । उत । उभयेन । एव । अस्मै । दुहे । दातुम् । च । इत् । अशकत् । वशाम् ॥४.१८॥

items.samhita_patha: दु॑रद॒भ्नैन॒मा श॑ये याचि॒तां च॒ न दित्स॑ति। नास्मै॒ कामाः॒ समृ॑ध्यन्ते॒ यामद॑त्त्वा॒ चिकी॑र्षति ॥

commentaries.whitney: Door-damaging (?) lies she on him, if he is not willing to give her when asked for; he does not succeed in the desires which, without having given her, he would fain accomplish ( cikīrṣa- ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies the obviously necessary emendation of yā́m to yā́n in d ⌊so Ludwig⌋. As to duradabhnā́ at the beginning, see the note to vs. 4. That the conjectural rendering is extremely unsatisfactory is plain. Ppp. has instead, for a , duritavīnapāçaye; and, in c, d , apparently kāmas sam ṛdhyate yam ad- , thus supporting our emendation. ⌊In Ppp. this verse precedes our 18.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: दुरदभ्नैनमा शये याचितां च न दित्सति। नास्मै कामाः समृध्यन्ते यामदत्त्वा चिकीर्षति ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: दुरदभ्ना । एनम् । आ । शये । याचिताम् । च । न । दित्सति । न । अस्मै । कामा: । सम । ऋध्यन्ते । याम् । अदत्वा । चिकीर्षति ॥४.१९॥

items.samhita_patha: दे॒वा व॒शाम॑याच॒न्मुखं॑ कृ॒त्वा ब्राह्म॑णम्। तेषां॒ सर्वे॑षा॒मद॑द॒द्धेडं॒ न्ये᳡ति॒ मानु॑षः ॥

commentaries.whitney: The gods asked for the cow, having made the Brahman their mouth; the wrath ( héḍa ) of them all incurs ( ni-i ) the man ( mā́nuṣa ) who gives not.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies emendation in b to brāhmaṇám . Ppp. reads in a yācanti , which does not rectify the meter. ⌊Read devā́so? ⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: देवा वशामयाचन्मुखं कृत्वा ब्राह्मणम्। तेषां सर्वेषामददद्धेडं न्ये᳡ति मानुषः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: देवा: । वशाम् । अयाचन् । मुखम् । कृत्वा । ब्राह्मणम् । तेषाम् । सर्वेषाम् । अददत् । हेडम् । नि । एति । मानुष: ॥४.२०॥

items.samhita_patha: हेडं॑ पशू॒नां न्ये᳡ति ब्राह्म॒णेभ्योऽद॑दद्व॒शाम्। दे॒वानां॒ निहि॑तं भा॒गं मर्त्य॒श्चेन्नि॑प्रिया॒यते॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: He incurs the wrath of cattle ( paçú ) who gives not the cow to the Brahmans—if a mortal keeps to himself the deposited portion of the gods.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The saṁhitā -mss. accent in b brāhmaṇébhyo dadat , and the pada correspondingly adadat (instead of ádadat ). Our text makes the necessary emendation. Ppp. gives for d ṛtāse nu priyāyate . ⌊See note to 11, above.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: हेडं पशूनां न्ये᳡ति ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽददद्वशाम्। देवानां निहितं भागं मर्त्यश्चेन्निप्रियायते ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: हेडम् । पशूनाम् । नि । एति । ब्राह्मणेभ्य: । अददत् । वशाम् । देवानाम् । निऽहितम् । भागम् । मर्त्य: । च । इत् । निऽप्रिययते ॥४.२१॥

items.samhita_patha: यद॒न्ये श॒तं याचे॑युर्ब्राह्म॒णा गोप॑तिं व॒शाम्। अथै॑नां दे॒वा अ॑ब्रुवन्ने॒वं ह॑ वि॒दुषो॑ व॒शा ॥

commentaries.whitney: If a hundred other Brahmans should ask the cow of its master, yet ( átha ) the gods said of her: the cow is his who knoweth thus.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All our mss. save two (I. and [?] E.s.m.) read etām (without accent) in c ; our text follows the two.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदन्ये शतं याचेयुर्ब्राह्मणा गोपतिं वशाम्। अथैनां देवा अब्रुवन्नेवं ह विदुषो वशा ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यत् । अन्ये । शतम् । याचेयु: । ब्राह्मणा: । गोऽपतिम् । वशाम् । अथ । एनाम् । देवा: । अब्रुवन् । एवम् । ह । विदुष: । वशा॥४.२२॥

items.samhita_patha: य ए॒वं वि॒दुषे॑ऽद॒त्त्वाथा॒न्येभ्यो॒ दद॑द्व॒शाम्। दु॒र्गा तस्मा॑ अधि॒ष्ठाने॑ पृथि॒वी स॒हदे॑वता ॥
items.pada_patha: य: । ए॒वम् । वि॒दुषे॑ । अद॑त्त्वा । अथ॑ । अ॒न्येभ्य॑: । दद॑त् । व॒शाम् । दु॒:ऽगा । तस्मै॑ । अ॒धि॒ऽस्थाने॑ । पृ॒थि॒वी । स॒हऽदे॑वता ॥४.२३॥

commentaries.whitney: Whoever, not having given her to one who knoweth thus, then shall give the cow to others, hard to go upon for him in his station is the earth with its deity.
commentaries.whitney_notes: In b the pada -text has anyébhyaḥ: adadat , and the saṁhitā -mss. correspondingly -bhyo dadad v-; this is emended in our text to -bhyó ‘d- (as if ádadat , as in vs. 21); but a decidedly better emendation would be to -bhyo dádat , as translated. Ppp. reads anyasmāi d- , which favors this understanding of the pāda; it also combines tasmā ’dh- in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: य एवं विदुषेऽदत्त्वाथान्येभ्यो ददद्वशाम्। दुर्गा तस्मा अधिष्ठाने पृथिवी सहदेवता ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: य: । एवम् । विदुषे । अदत्त्वा । अथ । अन्येभ्य: । ददत् । वशाम् । दु:ऽगा । तस्मै । अधिऽस्थाने । पृथिवी । सहऽदेवता ॥४.२३॥

items.samhita_patha: दे॒वा व॒शाम॑याच॒न्यस्मि॒न्नग्रे॒ अजा॑यत। तामे॒तां वि॑द्या॒न्नार॑दः स॒ह दे॒वैरुदा॑जत ॥

commentaries.whitney: The gods asked the cow [of him] in whose possession she was first ( ágre ) born; that same one may Nārada know; together with the gods he drove her away.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The connection of c, d is obscure, and tempts to conjectural emendations; Ludwig suggests vidvā́n for vidyāt: 'knowing her to be such, Nārada together with the gods drove her away (as theirs)'; this is quite acceptable. Ppp. reads at the end udājitā . One or two of our mss. (D.R.p.m.) accent nāradáḥ . The Anukr. takes no notice of the lack of a syllable in a . ⌊Read devā́so as in 20?⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: देवा वशामयाचन्यस्मिन्नग्रे अजायत। तामेतां विद्यान्नारदः सह देवैरुदाजत ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: देवा: । वशाम् । अयाचन् । यस्मिन् । अग्रे । अजायत । ताम् । एताम् । विद्यात् । नारद: । सह । देवै: । उत् । आजत ॥४.२४॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॑नप॒त्यमल्प॑पशुं व॒शा कृ॑णोति॒ पूरु॑षम्। ब्रा॑ह्म॒णैश्च॑ याचि॒तामथै॑नां निप्रिया॒यते॑ ॥
items.pada_patha: अ॒न॒प॒त्यम् । अल्प॑ऽपशुम् । व॒शा । कृ॒णो॒ति॒ । पुरु॑षम् । ब्रा॒ह्म॒णै: । च॒ । या॒चि॒ताम् । अथ॑ । ए॒ना॒म् । नि॒ऽप्रि॒य॒यते॑ ॥४.२५॥

commentaries.whitney: The cow makes a man ( pū́ruṣa ) destitute of descendants, poor in cattle, if, when she is asked for by the Brahmans, then he keeps her to himself.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b pāuruṣam , and in d nu priyāyata . The Anukr. takes no notice of any deficiency in c ; we may best resolve bṛ-āh- . ⌊Read brāhmaṇébhiç? ⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: अनपत्यमल्पपशुं वशा कृणोति पूरुषम्। ब्राह्मणैश्च याचितामथैनां निप्रियायते ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अनपत्यम् । अल्पऽपशुम् । वशा । कृणोति । पुरुषम् । ब्राह्मणै: । च । याचिताम् । अथ । एनाम् । निऽप्रिययते ॥४.२५॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒ग्नीषो॑माभ्यां॒ कामा॑य मि॒त्राय॒ वरु॑णाय च। तेभ्यो॑ याचन्ति ब्राह्म॒णास्तेष्वा वृ॑श्च॒तेऽद॑दत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: For Agni-and-Soma, for Love ( kā́ma ), for Mitra and for Varuṇa—for these the Brahmans ask her; under their wrath falls he who gives not.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अग्नीषोमाभ्यां कामाय मित्राय वरुणाय च। तेभ्यो याचन्ति ब्राह्मणास्तेष्वा वृश्चतेऽददत् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अग्नीषोमाभ्याम् । कामाय । मित्राय । वरुणाय । च । तेभ्य: । याचन्ति । ब्राह्मणा: । तेषु । आ । वृश्चते । अददत् ॥४.२६॥

items.samhita_patha: याव॑दस्या॒ गोप॑ति॒र्नोप॑शृणु॒यादृचः॑ स्व॒यम्। चरे॑दस्य॒ ताव॒द्गोषु॒ नास्य॑ श्रु॒त्वा गृ॒हे व॑सेत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: So long as the master of her should not himself overhear the verses ( ṛ́ç ), so long may she go about among his kine ( gó ); she may not abide in his house after he has heard.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies the evidently necessary emendation of vaçet at the end to vaset; R., indeed, has the latter; ⌊and so have 8 of SPP's authorities, against 7 with vaçet;⌋ Ppp. is corrupt: nā ’sya çrutā gṛhe sya . The Anukr. takes no notice of any redundancy in b ; but it can hardly expect us to make a pada -division between no and ’paçṛṇuyāt . The 'verses' are doubtless those with which the Brahmans come to claim their rightful property.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यावदस्या गोपतिर्नोपशृणुयादृचः स्वयम्। चरेदस्य तावद्गोषु नास्य श्रुत्वा गृहे वसेत् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यावत् । अस्या: । गोऽपति: । न । उपऽशृणुयात् । ऋच: । स्वयम् । चरेत् । अस्य । तावत् । गोषु । न । अस्य । श्रुत्वा । गृहे । वसेत् ॥४.२७॥

items.samhita_patha: यो अ॑स्या॒ ऋच॑ उप॒श्रुत्याथ॒ गोष्वची॑चरत्। आयु॑श्च॒ तस्य॒ भूतिं॑ च दे॒वा वृ॑श्चन्ति हीडि॒ताः ॥

commentaries.whitney: If any one, having overheard the verses of her, has then made her go about among his kine ( gó ), both the life-time and the growth of him do the gods, made wrathful, cut off ( vraçc ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Nearly all our mss. (E. has ácī- ) ⌊and all of SPP's⌋ leave acīcarat in b unaccented; and then, as if by way of compensation, they mostly (except Bs.s.m.D.R.) accent vṛ́çcanti .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यो अस्या ऋच उपश्रुत्याथ गोष्वचीचरत्। आयुश्च तस्य भूतिं च देवा वृश्चन्ति हीडिताः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: य: । अस्या: । ऋच: । उपऽश्रुत्य । अथ । गोषु । अचीचरत् । आयु: । च । तस्य । भूतिम् । च । देवा: । वृश्चन्ति । हीडिता: ॥४.२८॥

items.samhita_patha: व॒शा चर॑न्ती बहु॒धा दे॒वानां॒ निहि॑तो नि॒धिः। आ॒विष्कृ॑णुष्व रू॒पाणि॑ य॒दा स्थाम॒ जिघां॑सति ॥

commentaries.whitney: The cow, going about variously, the deposited deposit of the gods, manifests her forms, when she desires to go (?) to her station ( sthā́man ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, her rightful and appointed place. The translation implies in b the reading kṛnute instead of kṛṇuṣva , although the former is found only in O.p.m.D.T. ( -uti ). ⌊Three of SPP's pada -mss. have kṛṇute .⌋ The comm. to Prāt. ii. 63 quotes āviṣ kṛṇute rūpāṇi , which is not found in the text unless here. The translation also implies at the end jigāṅsati . The Prāt. (i. 86) seems to imply the occurrence in the text of such forms, and the sense obviously calls for them here and in the next verse; see the note to Prāt. i. 86. Ppp. reads in d yathā for yadā .

items.samhita_patha_plain: वशा चरन्ती बहुधा देवानां निहितो निधिः। आविष्कृणुष्व रूपाणि यदा स्थाम जिघांसति ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: वशा । चरन्ती । बहुऽधा । देवानाम् । निऽहित: । निऽधि: । आवि: । कृणुष्व । रूपाणि। यदा । स्थाम । जिघांसति ॥४.२९॥

items.samhita_patha: आ॒विरा॒त्मानं॑ कृणुते य॒दा स्थाम॒ जिघां॑सति। अथो॑ ह ब्र॒ह्मभ्यो॑ व॒शा या॒च्ञाय॑ कृणुते॒ मनः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: She manifests herself when she desires to go to her station; then the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋ makes up her mind for the asking of the priests ( brahmán ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, prepares herself to be asked for by them; brahmábhyas , dat. by attraction. ⌊Read again jígāṅsati : see note to vs. 29.⌋ Read in d yācñyā́ya , though the mss. mostly have -ñcy- , as they often blunder over such an unusual consonant-group. Ppp. reads uto for atho in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: आविरात्मानं कृणुते यदा स्थाम जिघांसति। अथो ह ब्रह्मभ्यो वशा याच्ञाय कृणुते मनः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: आवि: । आत्मानम्। कृणुते । यदा । स्थाम । जिघांसति । अथो इति । ह । ब्रह्मऽभ्य: । वशा । याञ्चाय । कृणुते । मन: ॥४.३०॥

items.samhita_patha: मन॑सा॒ सं क॑ल्पयति॒ तद्दे॒वाँ अपि॑ गच्छति। ततो॑ ह ब्र॒ह्माणो॑ व॒शामु॑प॒प्रय॑न्ति॒ याचि॑तुम् ॥
items.pada_patha: मन॑सा । सम् । क॒ल्प॒य॒ति॒ । तत् । दे॒वान् । अपि॑ । ग॒च्छ॒ति॒ । तत॑: । ह॒ । ब्र॒ह्माण॑: । व॒शाम् । उ॒प॒ऽप्रय॑न्ति । याचि॑तुम् ॥४.३१॥

commentaries.whitney: She plans ( sam-kḷp ) [it] with her mind; then she goes unto the gods; thence the priests ( brahmán ) go on to ask for the cow.

items.samhita_patha_plain: मनसा सं कल्पयति तद्देवाँ अपि गच्छति। ततो ह ब्रह्माणो वशामुपप्रयन्ति याचितुम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: मनसा । सम् । कल्पयति । तत् । देवान् । अपि । गच्छति । तत: । ह । ब्रह्माण: । वशाम् । उपऽप्रयन्ति । याचितुम् ॥४.३१॥

items.samhita_patha: स्व॑धाका॒रेण॑ पि॒तृभ्यो॑ य॒ज्ञेन॑ दे॒वता॑भ्यः। दाने॑न राज॒न्यो᳡ व॒शाया॑ मा॒तुर्हेडं॒ न ग॑च्छति ॥

commentaries.whitney: By offering of svadhā́ to the Fathers, by sacrifice to the deities, by giving of the cow, the noble ( rājanyà ) does not incur ( gam ) the mother's wrath.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads devebhyaḥ at end of b . The description of the Anukr. very unnecessarily forbids us to resolve -bhi-aḥ in b .

items.samhita_patha_plain: स्वधाकारेण पितृभ्यो यज्ञेन देवताभ्यः। दानेन राजन्यो᳡ वशाया मातुर्हेडं न गच्छति ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: स्वधाऽकारेण । पितृऽभ्य: । यज्ञेन । देवताभ्य: । दानेन । राजन्य᳡: । वशाया: । मातु: । हेडम् । न । गच्छति ॥४.३२॥

items.samhita_patha: व॒शा मा॒ता रा॑ज॒न्य᳡स्य॒ तथा॒ संभू॑तमग्र॒शः। तस्या॑ आहु॒रन॑र्पणं॒ यद्ब्र॒ह्मभ्यः॑ प्रदी॒यते॑ ॥
items.pada_patha: व॒शा । मा॒ता । रा॒ज॒न्य᳡स्य । तथा॑ । सम्ऽभू॑तम् । अ॒ग्र॒ऽश: । तस्या॑: । आ॒हु॒: । अन॑र्पणम् । यत् । ब्र॒ह्मऽभ्य॑: । प्र॒ऽदी॒यते॑ ॥४.३३॥

commentaries.whitney: The cow is mother of the noble; so came it (n.) into being in the beginning; they call it a non-abandonment (? ánarpaṇa ) of her that she is presented to the priests ( brahmán ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Pet. Lexx. render the difficult ánarpaṇa by 'a not giving away'; Ludwig, by 'no restitution.' Ppp. combines tasyā ”hur in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: वशा माता राजन्य᳡स्य तथा संभूतमग्रशः। तस्या आहुरनर्पणं यद्ब्रह्मभ्यः प्रदीयते ॥

items.samhita_patha: यथाज्यं॒ प्रगृ॑हीतमालु॒म्पेत्स्रु॒चो अ॒ग्नये॑। ए॒वा ह॑ ब्र॒ह्मभ्यो॑ व॒शाम॒ग्नय॒ आ वृ॑श्च॒तेऽद॑दत् ॥
items.pada_patha: यथा॑ । आज्य॑म् । प्रऽगृ॑हीतम् । आ॒ऽलु॒म्पेत्‌ । स्रु॒च: । अ॒ग्नये॑ । ए॒व । ह॒ । ब्र॒ह्मऽभ्य॑: । व॒शाम् । अ॒ग्नये॑ । आ। वृ॒श्च॒ते॒ । अद॑दत् ॥४.३४॥

commentaries.whitney: As one might snatch (? ā-lup ) from the spoon sacrificial butter held forth for the fire, so he who gives not the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋ ⌊to the priests⌋ falls under the wrath of Agni.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Perhaps, 'as [the fire] might snatch,' etc.—seizing on the butter before it is duly offered. Ppp. reads for a yad ājyaṁ pratijāgrāha , and in d omits a , thus rectifying the meter. The Anukr. takes no notice of the redundant syllable in our text; we are doubtless to get rid of it by contracting to agnáy’ ā́ . ⌊Were emendation necessary, one might be tempted to suggest agnā́v ā́: but cf. note to vs. 6 b .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: यथाज्यं प्रगृहीतमालुम्पेत्स्रुचो अग्नये। एवा ह ब्रह्मभ्यो वशामग्नय आ वृश्चतेऽददत् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यथा । आज्यम् । प्रऽगृहीतम् । आऽलुम्पेत्‌ । स्रुच: । अग्नये । एव । ह । ब्रह्मऽभ्य: । वशाम् । अग्नये । आ। वृश्चते । अददत् ॥४.३४॥

items.samhita_patha: पु॑रो॒डाश॑वत्सा सु॒दुघा॑ लो॒केऽस्मा॒ उप॑ तिष्ठति। सास्मै॒ सर्वा॒न्कामा॑न्व॒शा प्र॑द॒दुषे॑ दुहे ॥
items.samhita_patha_plain: पुरोडाशवत्सा सुदुघा लोकेऽस्मा उप तिष्ठति। सास्मै सर्वान्कामान्वशा प्रददुषे दुहे ॥

items.samhita_patha: सर्वा॒न्कामा॑न्यम॒राज्ये॑ व॒शा प्र॑द॒दुषे॑ दुहे। अथा॑हु॒र्नार॑कं लो॒कं नि॑रुन्धा॒नस्य॑ याचि॒ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: All his desires, in Yama's realm, does the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋ yield to him who has presented her; likewise they call hell the world of him who keeps her back when asked for.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text reads nárakam , and the difference of the two texts is noted in Prāt. iii. 21; iv. 90. Ppp. reads tathā for atha in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: सर्वान्कामान्यमराज्ये वशा प्रददुषे दुहे। अथाहुर्नारकं लोकं निरुन्धानस्य याचिताम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: सर्वान् । कामान्। यमऽराज्ये । वशा । प्रऽददुषे । दुहे ।अथ । आहु: । नरकम् । लोकम् । निऽरुन्धानस्य । याचिताम् ॥४.३६॥

items.samhita_patha: प्र॑वी॒यमा॑ना चरति क्रु॒द्धा गोप॑तये व॒शा। वे॒हतं॑ मा॒ मन्य॑मानो मृ॒त्योः पाशे॑षु बध्यताम् ॥
items.pada_patha: प्र॒ऽवी॒यमा॑ना । च॒र॒ति॒ । क्रु॒ध्दा । गोऽप॑तये । व॒शा । वे॒हत॑म्। मा॒ । मन्य॑मान: । मृ॒त्यो: । पाशे॑षु । ब॒ध्य॒ता॒म् ॥४.३७॥

commentaries.whitney: Being impregnated, the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋ goes about angry at her master: thinking me barren, let him be bound in the fetters of death.

items.samhita_patha_plain: प्रवीयमाना चरति क्रुद्धा गोपतये वशा। वेहतं मा मन्यमानो मृत्योः पाशेषु बध्यताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney:
And he who, thinking her barren, cooks the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋ at home
( amā́ )—his sons and sons' sons also does Brihaspati cause to be asked for.}}
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b , for amā ca , the equivalent gṛheṣu; further, in c, d , asya svaputrān pāutrāç cātayate bṛh- . ⌊Over "at home" W. interlines "in private": see vs. 53.⌋

commentaries.whitney: She sends down great heat, going about a cow ( gó ) among kine; further, to the master who has not given her the cow ( vaçā́ ) milks poison.
commentaries.whitney_notes: In b , apparently, 'being treated as an ordinary cow.' The 'milks' in d does not necessarily mean that she gives actual milk. Ppp. reads tato in c , for atho ha , thus rectifying the meter; the Anukr. takes no notice of the redundancy of the pāda, caused by the apparently intrusive ha .

items.samhita_patha_plain: महदेषाव तपति चरन्ती गोषु गौरपि। अथो ह गोपतये वशाददुषे विषं दुहे ॥

commentaries.whitney:
It is a thing dear to the cattle that she is presented to the priests
( brahmán ); further, that is a thing dear to the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋, that she be an oblation to the gods.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Lit. 'among the gods' (p. deva॰trā́ ).

items.samhita_patha_plain: प्रियं पशूनां भवति यद्ब्रह्मभ्यः प्रदीयते। अथो वशायास्तत्प्रियं यद्देवत्रा हविः स्यात् ॥

items.samhita_patha: या व॒शा उ॒दक॑ल्पयन्दे॒वा य॒ज्ञादु॒देत्य॑। तासां॑ विलि॒प्त्यं भी॒मामु॒दाकु॑रुत नार॒दः ॥

commentaries.whitney: What cows the gods shaped out ( ut-kḷp ), rising up from the sacrifice, of them Nārada selected for himself the fearful viliptī́ .
commentaries.whitney_notes: The root kḷp ( kalpay- ) with ud occurs nowhere else. In c , P.M.W.I.E.p.m.R. read viliptī́m , which would be the more normal accus. of -tī́ , but the meter is against it. But the accent -tyám is entirely inadmissible; it must be emended to -tyàm; ⌊cf. JAOS. x. 379. 369⌋. What sort of a cow ( vaçā́ ) is intended by viliptī́ (which ought to signify 'smeared over') is altogether obscure. Ppp. reads instead vilapatiṁ .

items.samhita_patha_plain: या वशा उदकल्पयन्देवा यज्ञादुदेत्य। तासां विलिप्त्यं भीमामुदाकुरुत नारदः ॥

items.samhita_patha: तां दे॒वा अ॑मीमांसन्त व॒शेया३मव॒शेति॑। ताम॑ब्रवीन्नार॒द ए॒षा व॒शानां॑ व॒शत॒मेति॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: The gods questioned ( mīmāṅs- ) about her: is this a cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋, or not a cow.' Of her Nārada said: she is of cows the most truly cow ( vaçátama ).

items.samhita_patha_plain: तां देवा अमीमांसन्त वशेया३मवशेति। तामब्रवीन्नारद एषा वशानां वशतमेति ॥

items.samhita_patha: कति॒ नु व॒शा ना॑रद॒ यास्त्वं वे॑त्थ मनुष्य॒जाः। तास्त्वा॑ पृच्छामि वि॒द्वांसं॒ कस्या॒ नाश्नी॑या॒दब्रा॑ह्मणः ॥

commentaries.whitney: How many, pray ( nú ), Nārada, are the cows which thou knowest, born among men ( manuṣyà- )? those I ask of thee who knowest; of which may a non-Brahman not partake ( aç )?
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for c , katimā ”sāṁ bhīmatamā (like our vs. 45 c ).

items.samhita_patha_plain: कति नु वशा नारद यास्त्वं वेत्थ मनुष्यजाः। तास्त्वा पृच्छामि विद्वांसं कस्या नाश्नीयादब्राह्मणः ॥

items.samhita_patha: वि॑लि॒प्त्या बृ॑हस्पते॒ या च॑ सू॒तव॑शा व॒शा। तस्या॒ नाश्नी॑या॒दब्रा॑ह्मणो॒ य आ॒शंसे॑त॒ भूत्या॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: The viliptī́ , O Brihaspati, and the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋ that has given birth to [such] a cow—of that one a non-Brahman who should hope for prosperity ( bhū́ti ) may not partake.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies at the beginning emendation to viliptī́ yā́ (as in vs. 46); the proper reading might also be viliptyàs , nom. pl.; -tyā́s seems inadmissible; Ppp. reads vilaptyā (for -ās? ). Ppp. has further tāsāṁ for tasyās in c . Sūtávaçā is rendered according to the requirement of the accent; the Pet. Lexx. define as 'a cow remaining barren after the birth of one calf'; and the legends told in explanation of the name in TS. vi. 1. 3 6 and MS. ii. 5. 4 support that understanding. ⌊Cf. Henry's translation, p. 208, and note, p. 256.⌋ Pāda c is redundant in this verse, as are also 46 c and 43 d ; the Anukr. heeds none of these cases.

items.samhita_patha_plain: विलिप्त्या बृहस्पते या च सूतवशा वशा। तस्या नाश्नीयादब्राह्मणो य आशंसेत भूत्याम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: नम॑स्ते अस्तु नारदानु॒ष्ठु वि॒दुषे॑ व॒शा। क॑त॒मासां॑ भी॒मत॑मा॒ यामद॑त्त्वा परा॒भवे॑त् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Homage be to thee, O Nārada; [be] the cow to him who at once knows it. Which one of them is the most fearful, not having given which, one would perish?
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in a te ‘stu , and in b vaçām , which is easier (Ludwig translates ⌊as if the text were vaçā́ḥ ⌋). In d , our text might better read ádattvā .

items.samhita_patha_plain: नमस्ते अस्तु नारदानुष्ठु विदुषे वशा। कतमासां भीमतमा यामदत्त्वा पराभवेत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: She that is viliptī́ , O Brihaspati, further the cow that has given birth to [such] a cow—of that one a non-Brahman who should hope for prosperity may not partake.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads at the beginning viluptiṁ bṛhaspataye yā ca sū- , and in c again (as in vs. 44) tāsāṁ .

items.samhita_patha_plain: विलिप्ती या बृहस्पतेऽथो सूतवशा वशा। तस्या नाश्नीयादब्राह्मणो य आशंसेत भूत्याम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: त्रीणि॒ वै व॑शाजा॒तानि॑ विलि॒प्ती सू॒तव॑शा व॒शा। ताः प्र य॑च्छेद्ब्र॒ह्मभ्यः॒ सो᳡ना॑व्र॒स्कः प्र॒जाप॑तौ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Three verily are the kinds of cow: the vilipti, she that has given birth to [such] a cow, the [simple] cow yagd; these one should present to the priests (brahman), [then] he falls not under the wrath of Prajapati.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. once more reads vilitptīs sū- in b ; it is easier to conjecture a meaning for viluptī than for viliptī . Most of our saṁhitā -mss. accent só ‘nāv- in d ; our text makes the necessary correction to sò . The irregularities of b and c are unnoticed in the Anukr.; ⌊or rather, it lets them balance each the other⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: त्रीणि वै वशाजातानि विलिप्ती सूतवशा वशा। ताः प्र यच्छेद्ब्रह्मभ्यः सो᳡नाव्रस्कः प्रजापतौ ॥

items.samhita_patha: ए॒तद्वो॑ ब्राह्मणा ह॒विरिति॑ मन्वीत याचि॒तः। व॒शां चेदे॑नं॒ याचे॑यु॒र्या भी॒माद॑दुषो गृ॒हे ॥

commentaries.whitney: This, O Brahmans, is your oblation—so, when asked ⌊therefor⌋, should he think, if they should ask of him the cow, which in the house of him who has not given her is fearful.

items.samhita_patha_plain: एतद्वो ब्राह्मणा हविरिति मन्वीत याचितः। वशां चेदेनं याचेयुर्या भीमाददुषो गृहे ॥

items.samhita_patha: दे॒वा व॒शां पर्य॑वद॒न्न नो॑ऽदा॒दिति॑ हीडि॒ताः। ए॒ताभि॑रृ॒ग्भिर्भे॒दं तस्मा॒द्वै स परा॑भवत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: The gods talked about the cow in wrath, saying: he hath not given it to us; with these verses ( ṛ́c ) [they talked about] Bheda; therefore indeed he perished.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads upa for pari in a , and, for b , sa no rājata heḍitā; and in c it rectifies the meter by giving bhedasya . The Anukr. does not heed the deficiency in our verse.

items.samhita_patha_plain: देवा वशां पर्यवदन्न नोऽदादिति हीडिताः। एताभिरृग्भिर्भेदं तस्माद्वै स पराभवत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: And Bheda gave her not, when asked by Indra for the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋; for that offense the gods cut him off in the contest for superiority.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Some of our mss. (Bp.E.D.K.) read etām (unaccented) in a ; nearly all (not Bs.s.m.D.) accent āgasó ‘vṛçcan in d . Ppp. has at the beginning utāi ’tāṁ bh-; its second half-verse is corrupt.

commentaries.whitney: They who, wheedling, advise ( vad ) to the non-giving of the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋, the villains fall under the fury of Indra through ignorance.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines in a vaçāyā ’dā- , and in c-d jālmā ”vṛç- .

commentaries.whitney: They who, leading away her master, then say: do not give—they, through ignorance, go to meet the hurled missile of Rudra.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Pari yanti is rendered as if prati y- , for which it is perhaps a misreading. Ppp. reads cetasas for acittyā . Part of our mss. (Bp.R.K.) leave āhus unaccented, and all have te instead of té in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: ये गोपतिं पराणीयाथाहुर्मा ददा इति। रुद्रस्यास्तां ते हेतिं परि यन्त्यचित्त्या ॥

items.samhita_patha: यदि॑ हु॒तां यद्यहु॑ताम॒मा च॒ पच॑ते व॒शाम्। दे॒वान्त्सब्रा॑ह्मणानृ॒त्वा जि॒ह्मो लो॒कान्निरृ॑च्छति ॥

commentaries.whitney: If as offered ( hu ) and if as unoffered one cooks the cow ⌊ vaçā́ ⌋ in private ( amā́ ), coming into collision with the gods accompanied by the Brahmans, he goes supine ( jihmá ) out of the world.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All the saṁhitā -mss. curiously read in c sábrāhmaṇānn (O. -ṇāṁn ) ṛtvā́; the pada -text has sá॰brāhmaṇān: ṛtvā́ . ⌊For amā́ , cf. vs. 38.⌋ ⌊Here ends the fourth anuvāka , with 1 hymn and 53 verses. The quoted Anukr. says saptabhir ūnā tu “vaçāḥ ," i.e. 'the cows[-hymn] is a [sixty] deficient by seven.'⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदि हुतां यद्यहुताममा च पचते वशाम्। देवान्त्सब्राह्मणानृत्वा जिह्मो लोकान्निरृच्छति ॥

commentaries.whitney: By toil, by penance [is she] created, acquired by bráhman , supported ( çritá ) on righteousness.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All our saṁhitā -mss. combine vittá rté . The appearance of meter in the verse (8 + 8) is perhaps not accidental; but there is no metrical structure elsewhere in the section.

commentaries.whitney: Covered with truth, enclosed with fortune, enveloped with glory.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Why the verse is called sāmnī rather than prājāpatyā , like its predecessor, cannot be told. The pada -text does not divide prā́vṛtā , although, in the apparently parallel case, it divides pári॰vṛtā .

items.samhita_patha_plain: सत्येनावृता श्रिया प्रावृता यशसा परीवृता ॥

commentaries.whitney: Set about with svadhā́ , surrounded with faith, guarded by consecration, standing firm in the offering, the world her post ( nidhána ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -mss. absurdly write práti॰stitāḥ (instead of -tā ). The metrical description of the Anukr. is not less absurd; to make the required 30 syllables, we have to resolve pári-ūḍhā .

commentaries.whitney: Bráhman her guide, the Brahman her over-lord.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines brāhmaṇo adh- . The á- needs to be restored in order to make the 13 syllables required by the definition of the Anukr.

commentaries.whitney: Of the Kshatriya who takes to himself that Brahman-cow, who scathes the Brahman,—
commentaries.whitney_notes: [ Atharvācārya.*—sapta paryāyāḥ. brahmagavīdevatāḥ. ] ⌊Partly metrical: vss. 15-17, 47-53, 55-70 are so reckoned by W. in the Index , p. 6.⌋ Found also in the main in Pāipp. xvi., but in the central parts with omissions and disorder of which the details are not given; ⌊vss. 58, 60, 64-73 are wanting⌋. Not quoted at all by Vāit., nor probably by Kāuç., since 'the two Brahman-cow hymns' mentioned in Kāuç. 48. 13 are doubtless v. 18, 19; although the comm. ⌊Dārila: cf. Keçava, p. 351 20 ⌋ declares these ⌊v. 18, 19⌋ to constitute one of the 'two,' and xii. 5 the other. *⌊The Berlin ms. reads prāguktarṣibrahmagavīdevatāḥ: so also SPP's citation, Critical Notice, p. 21. This seems to mean that Kaçyapa is the ṛṣi; h. 4 clearly has the same "deity" as this.⌋ Translated: Muir, i 2 . 288 (vss. 4-15); Ludwig, p. 529 (vss. 47-73); Henry, 209, 257; Griffith, ii. 127.

items.samhita_patha: अप॑ क्रामति सू॒नृता॑ वी॒र्यं१॒॑ पुण्या॑ ल॒क्ष्मीः ॥

commentaries.whitney: There departs the happiness ( sunṛ́tā ), the heroism, the good luck.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊The London Anukr. text reads prathamā bhāu prājāpatyānuṣṭu pakrāmatīti (vs. 6) satyena (etc., vs. 2): may be the pratīka of vs. 6 is misplaced and should be put before [ u ] bhāu (vs. 6 can be stretched to 16 syllables), or else the definition of 6 is fallen out.⌋ Ppp. reads puṇyalakṣmī . [ Paryāya II. — pañca. 7. sāmnī triṣṭubh; 8, 9. ārcy anuṣṭubh (8. bhurij); 10. uṣṇih; ⌊ 7-10. 1-p.: see under vs. 11;⌋ 11. ārcī nicṛt pan̄kti. ]

commentaries.whitney: Both force, and brilliancy, and power, and strength, and speech, and sense ( indriyá ), and fortune, and virtue ( dhárma ),—
